cases.note: The loop iterates the same unit thresholds (PB→KB) in the same order with the same 'B' fallback, so unit selection is identical to the original if/else chain.

The diff replaces `[-+]?0b` with `[^-+]?0b` in the core schema's explicit integer pattern, so explicitly tagged binary integers like `!!int 0b101` (and `-0b101`) now fail to resolve and throw, whereas the original accepted them.

cases.note: Pure refactor: 'rest' is digits.slice(2), used only in the same 0b/0o/0x branches where the original called value.slice(2); the decimal path is unchanged. No observable behavioural difference.
Dropping the type === 'string' check means non-string values without .length (e.g. undefined, null, numbers) hit `val.length` and throw a TypeError instead of the library's documented Error message.
